English: Stone Bath
A simple pit lined with stones, filled with clean water and used for basic ritual washing among the Israelite nomads.
Water Storage
Animal-skin cisterns and clay jars help preserve precious water for ritual use, ensuring the clans ability to maintain purity.
Ritual Pool
A purpose-dug pool, lined and protected, allowing for more thorough ritual immersion for the clans faithful.
Heated Chamber
A tented room warmed by stones and embers, allowing ritual bathing in comfort even in winter or harsh climates.
Changing Room
A wooden structure for undressing and preparing for immersion, helping maintain separation and propriety.
Private Bath Pavilion
A tented or wooden enclosure reserved for elders and respected families, enhancing unity and privacy for ritual cleansing.
Community Bathhouse
A permanent bathhouse of stone and wood, with separate pools for men and women. It is the heart of ritual purity for the entire clan.
Family Bath Hall
A grand building, richly decorated, with chambers for families to perform purification rites together, strengthening ties and unity.
Sanctified Bath Room
A consecrated chamber, adorned with ritual vessels and scripture, reinforcing the clans devotion and purity in the eyes of all.
Israelite Mikveh
A grand, flowing mikveh constructed to the highest standards of ritual law, drawing travelers and scholars to the clan for guidance.
